correctness.rationale: The Kearnes-Moorhead-Szendrei dichotomy excludes the G-set case because vector addition is essentially binary; in the vector-space case every polynomial operation is affine, and multilinearity at the original additive zero forces all coefficients and hence every higher-arity basic operation to vanish. The converse is ordinary vector-space freeness.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Targeted searches and inspection of the recent classification plus the closest classical linear-algebra sources did not locate the finite-field locally finite collapse for arbitrary identities. Burgin's homogeneous-identity results and older terminology remain residual prior-art risks.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp all-at-once rigidity result for finite-field multilinear algebra varieties, an exact classification in the one-product case, and a no-go theorem for unital locally finite Schreier algebra varieties.
